$comment: Canonical biomarker reference dataset. Committed and HUMAN-REVIEWABLE. Seeded into the canonical_biomarkers table (source='seed') and used as (1) the controlled vocabulary the AI reuses when canonicalizing names, and (2) the reference/optimal bands drawn on biomarker charts. Ranges are general adult values for an unconverted canonical unit. direction: 'higher_better' | 'lower_better' | 'in_range'. ref_* is a lab's standard reference range; optimal_* reflects general longevity literature for adults. Any field may be null (one-sided ranges are fine). Each entry may include 'conversions' (alternate-unit -> factor, where value_in_alt * factor = value in the canonical unit). Regenerate with `npm run gen:biomarkers`. INFORMATIONAL, NOT MEDICAL ADVICE — ranges may be inaccurate and often vary by sex/age.

biomarkers.name: Glucose
biomarkers.note: Serum or plasma glucose drawn without a stated fasting state. Whether this draw was fasting is not recorded, and the fasting and non-fasting bands differ by roughly 40 mg/dL at the top of normal. The value is shown but not flagged, because either band would be a guess. A draw the document states as fasting belongs under Glucose, Fasting, which carries the 70–99 mg/dL band.

biomarkers.name: PhenoAge
biomarkers.note: Levine Phenotypic Age (2018), in years — a derived biological-age estimate from 9 analytes (albumin, creatinine, glucose, hs-CRP, lymphocyte %, MCV, RDW, ALP, WBC) plus chronological age. Interpreted relative to chronological age (lower = biologically younger); a population estimate with several years of error, not day-level precision.

biomarkers.name: Triglyceride/HDL Ratio
biomarkers.note: Derived from the lipid panel (Triglycerides ÷ HDL, both mg/dL). Surrogate for insulin resistance / small-dense LDL; <2 favorable, ≥3.5 suggests insulin resistance. mg/dL-based — a mmol/L ratio differs.

biomarkers.name: Neutrophils, Absolute
biomarkers.note: Absolute neutrophil count (ANC). Adult ~1.5–8.0 ×10^3/uL; varies by age (see age bands).

biomarkers.name: Lymphocytes, Absolute
biomarkers.note: Absolute lymphocyte count (ALC). Adult ~1.0–4.8 ×10^3/uL; much higher in infancy/childhood (see age bands).

biomarkers.name: Monocytes, Relative
biomarkers.note: Monocytes as a fraction of leukocytes (relative count). Companion to the absolute 'Monocytes' (cells/uL) entry.

biomarkers.name: Eosinophils, Relative
biomarkers.note: Eosinophils as a fraction of leukocytes (relative count). Companion to the absolute 'Eosinophils' (cells/uL) entry.

biomarkers.name: Basophils, Relative
biomarkers.note: Basophils as a fraction of leukocytes (relative count). Companion to the absolute 'Basophils' (cells/uL) entry.

biomarkers.name: Nucleated Red Blood Cells, Relative
biomarkers.note: Nucleated (immature) red cells as a fraction of leukocytes (NRBC/100 WBC). Normally absent in children/adults; present at birth and clears within the first week (see infancy age band). Companion to the absolute NRBC count.

ranges_by_age.note: Term newborns normally show up to ~5–10 NRBC/100 WBC at birth, clearing within the first week; a whole-year band is coarse (it can UNDER-flag a genuinely raised NRBC later in infancy).

biomarkers.name: Nucleated Red Blood Cells, Absolute
biomarkers.note: Absolute nucleated-red-cell count (×10^3/uL). Normally ≈0 in children/adults; elevated at birth and clears within the first week (see infancy age band). Companion to the NRBC percentage.

ranges_by_age.note: Newborn absolute NRBC is elevated at birth and clears within the first week; a whole-year band is coarse.

biomarkers.name: Immature Granulocytes, Relative
biomarkers.note: Immature granulocytes (metamyelocytes/myelocytes/promyelocytes) as a fraction of leukocytes — a left-shift marker. Adult reference ~0.0–0.5% (Sysmex IG%); mildly higher in early infancy (see age band). Companion to the absolute IG count.

biomarkers.name: Immature Granulocytes, Absolute
biomarkers.note: Absolute immature-granulocyte count (×10^3/uL) — a left-shift marker. Adult reference ~0.00–0.03 (Sysmex IG#); mildly higher in early infancy (see age band). Companion to the IG percentage.

biomarkers.name: Hemoglobin A
biomarkers.note: Hemoglobin A (α2β2), the dominant adult hemoglobin, as a fraction of total hemoglobin on electrophoresis. The clinically meaningful abnormality is a REDUCED HbA (a structural/variant hemoglobinopathy displacing it), so only a lower bound is set. Physiologically LOW in infancy (fetal-hemoglobin switch).

biomarkers.name: Hemoglobin A2
biomarkers.note: Hemoglobin A2 (α2δ2) fraction on electrophoresis. An ELEVATED HbA2 (>~3.3%) is the classic marker of beta-thalassemia trait; a low HbA2 can accompany iron deficiency or alpha/delta-thalassemia. Adult range ~2.0–3.3%.

biomarkers.name: Hemoglobin F
biomarkers.note: Fetal hemoglobin (α2γ2) fraction on electrophoresis. Predominant at birth and normally falls to <~2% in adults; an elevated adult HbF occurs in hereditary persistence of fetal hemoglobin and some thalassemias/hemoglobinopathies. Physiologically HIGH in infancy (fetal-hemoglobin switch).

biomarkers.name: Thyroxine, Total (Total T4)
biomarkers.note: Total thyroxine. Elevated by high thyroxine-binding globulin (pregnancy, estrogen); Free T4 is more specific.

biomarkers.name: Triiodothyronine, Total (Total T3)
biomarkers.note: Total triiodothyronine.

biomarkers.name: Direct Bilirubin
biomarkers.note: Conjugated bilirubin.

biomarkers.name: Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH)
biomarkers.note: Assay-dependent; hemolyzed specimens read falsely high.

biomarkers.name: Creatine Kinase (CK)
biomarkers.note: Higher in males; transiently elevated by exercise/muscle injury and higher with greater muscle mass and in some ancestries.

biomarkers.name: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR)
biomarkers.note: Upper limit rises with age (roughly age/2 for men, (age+10)/2 for women), so this deliberately broad adult cutoff under-flags young adults rather than over-flag older ones.

biomarkers.name: Anion Gap
biomarkers.note: Varies widely by analyzer (direct-ISE methods run lower) and whether K+ is included in the calculation; range is intentionally broad.

biomarkers.name: Reticulocytes, Relative
biomarkers.note: Reticulocytes as a fraction of erythrocytes.

biomarkers.name: Reticulocytes, Absolute
biomarkers.note: Absolute reticulocyte count (~25–75 ×10^3/uL; equivalently 25–75 ×10^9/L). Assay-dependent.

biomarkers.name: Estradiol
biomarkers.note: Sex- and cycle-dependent (pg/mL). Female = reproductive-age, spanning follicular→mid-cycle peak→luteal (the app can't know cycle phase), with no low bound so early-follicular / post-menopausal lows never false-flag; the lower post-menopausal range is already covered, so no age band. Male ~10–40. Replaces a prior male-ish single range that false-flagged normal female physiology. When the profile's reproductive_status is set, ranges_by_status overrides this.

premenopausal.note: Reproductive-age envelope (follicular→mid-cycle→luteal); open low bound so early-follicular lows never false-flag.

postmenopausal.note: Postmenopausal E2 ≤~30 pg/mL; open low bound (HRT/atrophy lows aren't flagged). Lets a post-menopausal HIGH estradiol flag.

follicular.note: Follicular→ovulatory envelope (Mayo mid-cycle peak ~498 pg/mL); menstrual dates read this too.

biomarkers.name: Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH)
biomarkers.note: Sex- and life-stage-dependent (mIU/mL). Female reproductive-age spans luteal→mid-cycle (the app can't know cycle phase); post-menopausal FSH is many-fold higher and is resolved via the 51+ age band so it isn't false-flagged 'high'. When the profile's reproductive_status is set, ranges_by_status overrides the age proxy.

ranges_by_age.note: Post-menopausal (age ≥51, median menopause): FSH rises to ~27–133 mIU/mL; the low bound stays broad so HRT-suppressed values aren't false-flagged 'low'. Male ceiling widened for the age-related rise.

postmenopausal.note: Postmenopausal FSH up to ~134.8 mIU/mL (Mayo/ARUP); open low bound so HRT-suppressed values aren't false-flagged 'low'.

follicular.note: Follicular→ovulatory envelope (Mayo mid-cycle peak ~21.5 mIU/mL); menstrual dates read this too.

biomarkers.name: Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
biomarkers.note: Sex-dependent (mIU/mL). Female reproductive-age spans the luteal low → ovulatory LH surge (~95, and the app can't know cycle phase) — an envelope that already contains the post-menopausal range (~8–59), so LH needs no age band. Male ~1.5–9.5. When the profile's reproductive_status is set, ranges_by_status refines this.

postmenopausal.note: Postmenopausal LH up to ~58.5 mIU/mL (Mayo/endocrine); open low bound so HRT-suppressed values aren't false-flagged 'low'.

follicular.note: Follicular→ovulatory envelope carrying the LH surge (Mayo mid-cycle peak ~95.6 mIU/mL); menstrual dates read this too.

biomarkers.name: Progesterone
biomarkers.note: Cycle-phase-dependent (ng/mL). Female base is a reproductive envelope spanning follicular (≤~1.5) → mid-luteal peak (~24) since the app can't know cycle phase without a cycle log; open low so follicular/menstrual lows never false-flag. When the cycle log covers the collection date, ranges_by_cycle_phase refines it (follicular ≤1.5 vs luteal ≤24); when reproductive_status is set, ranges_by_status applies. Male ~≤1.4.

postmenopausal.note: Postmenopausal progesterone ≤~0.5 ng/mL (Mayo); open low bound. Lets a post-menopausal HIGH progesterone flag.

follicular.note: Follicular (and menstrual) progesterone ≤~1.5 ng/mL (Mayo). A value well above this on a follicular date is a genuine catch the coarse envelope misses.

luteal.note: Luteal-phase progesterone up to ~23.9 ng/mL (Mayo mid-luteal peak); a normal-luteal value is not flagged 'high'.

biomarkers.name: Grip Strength
biomarkers.note: Maximum handgrip (dynamometer), in kg. A whole-body strength proxy and independent mortality predictor; interpreted by age/sex percentile (Dodds et al. 2014), not a fixed cutoff.

biomarkers.name: 30-Second Chair Stand
biomarkers.note: Sit-to-stand repetitions in 30 seconds — a lower-body strength / frailty measure for older adults. Interpreted by age/sex percentile (Rikli & Jones Senior Fitness Test), not a fixed cutoff.

biomarkers.name: Single-Leg Balance
biomarkers.note: Unipedal stance time, eyes open (seconds; typically capped at 45 s). A postural-control / fall-risk measure; interpreted by age/sex percentile (Springer et al. 2007), not a fixed cutoff.

biomarkers.name: ABO Blood Group
biomarkers.note: ABO group (A, B, AB, or O). An immutable identity attribute — never flagged, never retested.

biomarkers.name: Rh Type
biomarkers.note: Rh(D) factor (positive or negative). An immutable identity attribute — never flagged, never retested.

biomarkers.name: Blood Type
biomarkers.note: Combined ABO group + Rh factor as one result (e.g. "O Positive"), the form many EHRs report. An immutable identity attribute — never flagged, never retested.

biomarkers.name: Protein, Urine
biomarkers.note: Urine dipstick protein — a screen for kidney involvement. Qualitative (Negative/Trace/1+…); Negative is normal. Distinct from serum Total Protein.

biomarkers.name: Glucose, Urine
biomarkers.note: Urine dipstick glucose — normally absent; present when blood glucose exceeds the renal threshold. Qualitative (Negative is normal). Distinct from serum Glucose.

biomarkers.name: Ketones, Urine
biomarkers.note: Urine dipstick ketones — a marker of fat metabolism, raised in fasting, low-carbohydrate states, or uncontrolled diabetes. Qualitative (Negative is normal).

biomarkers.name: Bilirubin, Urine
biomarkers.note: Urine dipstick bilirubin — normally absent; its presence points to liver or bile-duct disease. Qualitative (Negative is normal). Distinct from serum Total/Direct Bilirubin.

biomarkers.name: Blood, Urine
biomarkers.note: Urine dipstick (occult) blood — detects hemoglobin/myoglobin. Qualitative (Negative is normal). A microscopic red-cell count is the separate 'Red Blood Cells, Urine' entry.

biomarkers.name: Nitrite, Urine
biomarkers.note: Urine dipstick nitrite — a positive suggests bacteria that convert nitrate to nitrite (a urinary-tract infection clue). Qualitative (Negative is normal).

biomarkers.name: Leukocyte Esterase, Urine
biomarkers.note: Urine dipstick leukocyte esterase — an enzyme from white blood cells, a marker of urinary-tract inflammation/infection. Qualitative (Negative is normal).

biomarkers.name: Urobilinogen, Urine
biomarkers.note: Urine urobilinogen — a small amount (up to ~1 mg/dL) is normal; raised levels can reflect liver disease or hemolysis, and absence can reflect bile-duct obstruction.

biomarkers.name: Immunoglobulin G
biomarkers.note: Total serum IgG — the most abundant antibody class, reflecting long-term/adaptive immunity. Low levels can signal immunodeficiency; high levels chronic infection or inflammation.

biomarkers.name: Immunoglobulin A
biomarkers.note: Serum IgA — the antibody class guarding mucosal surfaces (gut, airways). Selective IgA deficiency is the most common primary immunodeficiency.

biomarkers.name: Immunoglobulin M
biomarkers.note: Serum IgM — the first antibody class produced in a new infection, so a rise can indicate a recent or acute exposure.

biomarkers.name: Immunoglobulin G Subclass 1
biomarkers.note: IgG1 — the largest IgG subclass, directed mainly at protein antigens. Measured in the workup of a suspected antibody deficiency.

biomarkers.name: Immunoglobulin G Subclass 2
biomarkers.note: IgG2 — the IgG subclass directed mainly at polysaccharide antigens (e.g. encapsulated bacteria). A selective deficiency can raise susceptibility to such infections.

biomarkers.name: Immunoglobulin G Subclass 3
biomarkers.note: IgG3 — an IgG subclass active against protein and viral antigens, with the shortest half-life of the four.

biomarkers.name: Immunoglobulin G Subclass 4
biomarkers.note: IgG4 — the least abundant IgG subclass; markedly elevated levels are associated with IgG4-related disease.

biomarkers.name: Leptin
biomarkers.note: Leptin is a hormone made by fat tissue that signals energy stores to the brain; levels track body-fat mass and are strongly sex- and BMI-dependent, so no single reference band applies.

biomarkers.name: Albumin, Urine
biomarkers.note: Urine albumin screens for early kidney damage. It is interpreted as the albumin-to-creatinine ratio (normal <30 mg/g), not a fixed concentration, so no band is set here. Distinct from serum Albumin.

biomarkers.name: Creatinine, Urine
biomarkers.note: Urine creatinine reflects urine concentration and is used mainly to normalize other urine analytes (as a ratio); its own level varies with hydration, so no reference band applies. Distinct from serum Creatinine.

biomarkers.name: Alpha-Fetoprotein (AFP)
biomarkers.note: AFP is a protein used as a tumor marker (notably for liver and germ-cell cancers) and, in pregnancy, a screening marker. In non-pregnant adults it is normally low.

biomarkers.name: Carcinoembryonic Antigen (CEA)
biomarkers.note: CEA is a tumor marker used mainly to monitor colorectal and some other cancers. Levels can also be mildly raised by smoking and some benign conditions. The reference cutoff is higher in smokers.

biomarkers.name: Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg)
biomarkers.note: HBsAg is a marker of active hepatitis B infection. It is reported qualitatively; a negative (non-reactive) result is normal, and a positive result indicates current infection.

biomarkers.name: Hepatitis B Surface Antibody (HBsAb)
biomarkers.note: HBsAb (anti-HBs) reflects immunity to hepatitis B from vaccination or past infection; a level at or above 10 mIU/mL is generally considered protective.

biomarkers.name: Hepatitis C Antibody (Anti-HCV)
biomarkers.note: Anti-HCV screens for exposure to hepatitis C. It is reported qualitatively; a non-reactive result is normal, and a reactive result prompts confirmatory HCV RNA testing.

biomarkers.name: BUN/Creatinine Ratio
biomarkers.note: The ratio of blood urea nitrogen to creatinine helps distinguish causes of kidney impairment and hydration status; it is a calculated value with no units.

biomarkers.name: LDL/HDL Ratio
biomarkers.note: The ratio of LDL to HDL cholesterol is a summary marker of cardiovascular risk; lower is better. It is a calculated value with no units.

biomarkers.name: Intraocular Pressure, Unspecified Eye
biomarkers.note: Fluid pressure inside the eye (tonometry), eye unspecified. Normal ~10–21 mmHg; above 21 is ocular hypertension, a glaucoma risk factor (not a diagnosis). AAO / Glaucoma Research Foundation.

biomarkers.name: Intraocular Pressure, Right Eye
biomarkers.note: Intraocular pressure of the right eye (OD), by tonometry. Normal ~10–21 mmHg; above 21 is ocular hypertension. Kept as a separate series from the left eye. AAO / Glaucoma Research Foundation.

biomarkers.name: Intraocular Pressure, Left Eye
biomarkers.note: Intraocular pressure of the left eye (OS), by tonometry. Normal ~10–21 mmHg; above 21 is ocular hypertension. Kept as a separate series from the right eye. AAO / Glaucoma Research Foundation.

biomarkers.name: Visual Acuity, Unspecified Eye
biomarkers.note: Clearness of vision, eye unspecified, as a Snellen fraction (e.g. 20/20; 6/6 metric). Qualitative — no numeric reference band, so it is trended as a dated timeline, never flagged.

biomarkers.name: Visual Acuity, Right Eye
biomarkers.note: Visual acuity of the right eye (OD) as a Snellen fraction (e.g. 20/20). Qualitative — no numeric reference band; trended as a dated timeline, never flagged. Kept as a separate series from the left eye.

biomarkers.name: Visual Acuity, Left Eye
biomarkers.note: Visual acuity of the left eye (OS) as a Snellen fraction (e.g. 20/20). Qualitative — no numeric reference band; trended as a dated timeline, never flagged. Kept as a separate series from the right eye.

biomarkers.name: Periodontal Probing Depth
biomarkers.note: Sulcus/pocket depth on periodontal probing, in millimetres (the deepest or a representative site). A healthy sulcus is ~1–3 mm; 4 mm and deeper indicates periodontal pocketing worth monitoring. American Academy of Periodontology.

biomarkers.name: Bleeding on Probing
biomarkers.note: Proportion of periodontal sites that bleed on gentle probing, as a full-mouth percentage. A full-mouth score under ~10% is consistent with periodontal stability; higher suggests active gingival inflammation. American Academy of Periodontology.

biomarkers.name: Clinical Attachment Loss
biomarkers.note: Distance from the cemento-enamel junction to the base of the periodontal pocket, in millimetres — the cumulative attachment lost. 1–2 mm is mild, 3–4 mm moderate, ≥5 mm severe (2017 AAP/EFP staging). Tracks periodontitis progression over time.

biomarkers.name: Hearing Threshold, Right Ear 250 Hz
biomarkers.note: Pure-tone air-conduction hearing threshold for the RIGHT ear at 250 Hz, in decibels hearing level (dB HL). Normal hearing is ≤25 dB HL (WHO); a higher number means the ear needs a louder tone to hear it. Its own per-ear, per-frequency audiogram series. American Speech-Language-Hearing Association / WHO.

biomarkers.name: Hearing Threshold, Right Ear 500 Hz
biomarkers.note: Pure-tone air-conduction hearing threshold for the RIGHT ear at 500 Hz, in decibels hearing level (dB HL). Normal hearing is ≤25 dB HL (WHO); a higher number means the ear needs a louder tone to hear it. Its own per-ear, per-frequency audiogram series. American Speech-Language-Hearing Association / WHO.

biomarkers.name: Hearing Threshold, Right Ear 1 kHz
biomarkers.note: Pure-tone air-conduction hearing threshold for the RIGHT ear at 1 kHz, in decibels hearing level (dB HL). Normal hearing is ≤25 dB HL (WHO); a higher number means the ear needs a louder tone to hear it. Its own per-ear, per-frequency audiogram series. American Speech-Language-Hearing Association / WHO.

biomarkers.name: Hearing Threshold, Right Ear 2 kHz
biomarkers.note: Pure-tone air-conduction hearing threshold for the RIGHT ear at 2 kHz, in decibels hearing level (dB HL). Normal hearing is ≤25 dB HL (WHO); a higher number means the ear needs a louder tone to hear it. Its own per-ear, per-frequency audiogram series. American Speech-Language-Hearing Association / WHO.

biomarkers.name: Hearing Threshold, Right Ear 4 kHz
biomarkers.note: Pure-tone air-conduction hearing threshold for the RIGHT ear at 4 kHz, in decibels hearing level (dB HL). Normal hearing is ≤25 dB HL (WHO); a higher number means the ear needs a louder tone to hear it — 4 kHz is the classic noise-notch frequency. Its own per-ear, per-frequency audiogram series. American Speech-Language-Hearing Association / WHO.

biomarkers.name: Hearing Threshold, Right Ear 8 kHz
biomarkers.note: Pure-tone air-conduction hearing threshold for the RIGHT ear at 8 kHz, in decibels hearing level (dB HL). Normal hearing is ≤25 dB HL (WHO); a higher number means the ear needs a louder tone to hear it. Its own per-ear, per-frequency audiogram series. American Speech-Language-Hearing Association / WHO.

biomarkers.name: Hearing Threshold, Left Ear 250 Hz
biomarkers.note: Pure-tone air-conduction hearing threshold for the LEFT ear at 250 Hz, in decibels hearing level (dB HL). Normal hearing is ≤25 dB HL (WHO); a higher number means the ear needs a louder tone to hear it. Its own per-ear, per-frequency audiogram series. American Speech-Language-Hearing Association / WHO.

biomarkers.name: Hearing Threshold, Left Ear 500 Hz
biomarkers.note: Pure-tone air-conduction hearing threshold for the LEFT ear at 500 Hz, in decibels hearing level (dB HL). Normal hearing is ≤25 dB HL (WHO); a higher number means the ear needs a louder tone to hear it. Its own per-ear, per-frequency audiogram series. American Speech-Language-Hearing Association / WHO.

biomarkers.name: Hearing Threshold, Left Ear 1 kHz
biomarkers.note: Pure-tone air-conduction hearing threshold for the LEFT ear at 1 kHz, in decibels hearing level (dB HL). Normal hearing is ≤25 dB HL (WHO); a higher number means the ear needs a louder tone to hear it. Its own per-ear, per-frequency audiogram series. American Speech-Language-Hearing Association / WHO.

biomarkers.name: Hearing Threshold, Left Ear 2 kHz
biomarkers.note: Pure-tone air-conduction hearing threshold for the LEFT ear at 2 kHz, in decibels hearing level (dB HL). Normal hearing is ≤25 dB HL (WHO); a higher number means the ear needs a louder tone to hear it. Its own per-ear, per-frequency audiogram series. American Speech-Language-Hearing Association / WHO.

biomarkers.name: Hearing Threshold, Left Ear 4 kHz
biomarkers.note: Pure-tone air-conduction hearing threshold for the LEFT ear at 4 kHz, in decibels hearing level (dB HL). Normal hearing is ≤25 dB HL (WHO); a higher number means the ear needs a louder tone to hear it — 4 kHz is the classic noise-notch frequency. Its own per-ear, per-frequency audiogram series. American Speech-Language-Hearing Association / WHO.

biomarkers.name: Hearing Threshold, Left Ear 8 kHz
biomarkers.note: Pure-tone air-conduction hearing threshold for the LEFT ear at 8 kHz, in decibels hearing level (dB HL). Normal hearing is ≤25 dB HL (WHO); a higher number means the ear needs a louder tone to hear it. Its own per-ear, per-frequency audiogram series. American Speech-Language-Hearing Association / WHO.

biomarkers.name: PHQ-9
biomarkers.note: Patient Health Questionnaire-9 total score (0–27), a validated screening instrument for depression severity. Severity bands: 0–4 minimal, 5–9 mild, 10–14 moderate, 15–19 moderately severe, 20–27 severe. Screening only, NOT a diagnosis. Item 9 asks about thoughts of self-harm. Public domain (Spitzer, Williams, Kroenke / Pfizer).

biomarkers.name: GAD-7
biomarkers.note: Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 total score (0–21), a validated screening instrument for anxiety severity. Severity bands: 0–4 minimal, 5–9 mild, 10–14 moderate, 15–21 severe. Screening only, NOT a diagnosis. Public domain (Spitzer, Kroenke, Williams, Löwe).

biomarkers.name: AUDIT-C
biomarkers.note: AUDIT-C total score (0–12), the 3-item alcohol-use screen (consumption items of the WHO AUDIT). Bands (UK PHE/NHS scoring): 0–4 lower risk, 5–7 increasing risk, 8–10 higher risk, 11–12 possible dependence; a score of 3+ (women) or 4+ (men) is commonly treated as a positive screen. Screening only, NOT a diagnosis. Public domain (Bush et al. 1998, VA).

biomarkers.name: AUDIT
biomarkers.note: AUDIT total score (0–40), the WHO 10-item Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test. Risk zones (WHO manual): 0–7 lower risk, 8–15 increasing risk, 16–19 higher risk, 20–40 possible dependence. Screening only, NOT a diagnosis. Recorded as an outside-administered total (item text not reproduced in-app).

biomarkers.name: DAST-10
biomarkers.note: Drug Abuse Screening Test (DAST-10) total score (0–10) for non-alcohol drug use in the past 12 months. Bands (Skinner): 0 none reported, 1–2 low, 3–5 moderate, 6–8 substantial, 9–10 severe. Screening only, NOT a diagnosis. Recorded as an outside-administered total (item text not reproduced in-app; © H. A. Skinner / CAMH).

biomarkers.name: Vitamin D2, 25-Hydroxy
biomarkers.note: 25-hydroxyvitamin D2 (ergocalciferol) fraction — its OWN trendable series, distinct from the total. No sufficiency band: a low D2 is normal for anyone not taking ergocalciferol, so vitamin-D status is assessed on the TOTAL 25-OH, never this fraction alone.

biomarkers.name: Vitamin D3, 25-Hydroxy
biomarkers.note: 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) fraction — its OWN trendable series, distinct from the total. No sufficiency band: vitamin-D status is assessed on the TOTAL 25-OH, never this fraction alone.

biomarkers.name: Vitamin D, 1,25-Dihydroxy
biomarkers.note: 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (calcitriol) — the ACTIVE hormone, distinct from the 25-OH storage form. Adult ~18–72 pg/mL. Used in hypercalcemia / sarcoidosis / CKD workups, NOT for routine vitamin-D status (which is the 25-OH total).

biomarkers.name: C-Reactive Protein
biomarkers.note: Standard-sensitivity CRP (acute inflammation/infection), mg/L — a DIFFERENT assay than hs-CRP (the CV-risk high-sensitivity test). ~<3 low, >10 suggests acute inflammation.

biomarkers.name: Glucose, Fasting
biomarkers.note: Fasting plasma glucose. ADA thresholds: 70–99 normal, 100–125 prediabetes, ≥126 diabetes (confirmed). Distinct from a random Glucose and from the A1c/eAG family.

biomarkers.name: Rapid Plasma Reagin (RPR)
biomarkers.note: Rapid plasma reagin — syphilis screen. Qualitative (Reactive/Non-Reactive); a reactive result is followed by a confirmatory treponemal test. No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: Hemoglobin Electrophoresis
biomarkers.note: Hemoglobinopathy screen (sickle-cell / thalassemia trait). Reported as an interpretation (e.g. Normal / abnormal variant pattern), not a measured quantity. No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: HIV Antigen/Antibody
biomarkers.note: HIV 4th-generation Ag/Ab combination screen. Qualitative (Reactive/Non-Reactive); a reactive result is confirmed by a supplemental assay. No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: SARS-CoV-2 NAAT
biomarkers.note: SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) nucleic-acid amplification (PCR). Qualitative (Detected/Not Detected). No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: SARS-CoV-2 Antigen
biomarkers.note: SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) rapid antigen test. Qualitative (Positive/Negative). No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: Influenza A NAAT
biomarkers.note: Influenza A virus nucleic-acid amplification (PCR). Qualitative (Detected/Not Detected). No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: Influenza B NAAT
biomarkers.note: Influenza B virus nucleic-acid amplification (PCR). Qualitative (Detected/Not Detected). No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: Influenza A Antigen
biomarkers.note: Influenza A rapid antigen test. Qualitative (Positive/Negative). No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: Influenza B Antigen
biomarkers.note: Influenza B rapid antigen test. Qualitative (Positive/Negative). No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: RSV NAAT
biomarkers.note: Respiratory syncytial virus nucleic-acid amplification (PCR). Qualitative (Detected/Not Detected). No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: Streptococcus A NAAT
biomarkers.note: Group A Streptococcus (pharyngitis) nucleic-acid amplification. Qualitative (Detected/Not Detected). No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: Group B Streptococcus
biomarkers.note: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) screen — routine in pregnancy. Qualitative (Detected/Not Detected). No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: Chlamydia trachomatis NAAT
biomarkers.note: Chlamydia trachomatis nucleic-acid amplification. Qualitative (Detected/Not Detected). No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: Neisseria gonorrhoeae NAAT
biomarkers.note: Neisseria gonorrhoeae nucleic-acid amplification. Qualitative (Detected/Not Detected). No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: HPV, High-Risk
biomarkers.note: High-risk human papillomavirus (pooled hrHPV) — cervical cancer screen. Qualitative (Positive/Negative). No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: HPV Genotype 16
biomarkers.note: HPV genotype 16 (a high-risk type). Qualitative (Positive/Negative). Kept distinct from the pooled hrHPV result and from genotype 18/45. No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: HPV Genotype 18/45
biomarkers.note: HPV genotype 18/45 (high-risk types). Qualitative (Positive/Negative). Kept distinct from the pooled hrHPV result and from genotype 16. No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: Culture Organism
biomarkers.note: The organism identified by a microbiology culture (the value is the organism name, e.g. "Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus"). Qualitative identity, not a measurement — no numeric band.

biomarkers.name: Rubella Antibody IgG
biomarkers.note: Rubella IgG — immunity marker. Reported qualitatively (Immune/Non-Immune) or as an assay-specific titer; immune is favorable. No universal numeric band (assay-specific).

biomarkers.name: Measles Antibody IgG
biomarkers.note: Measles (rubeola) IgG — immunity marker. Reported qualitatively (Immune/Non-Immune) or as an assay-specific titer; immune is favorable. No universal numeric band (assay-specific).

biomarkers.name: Mumps Antibody IgG
biomarkers.note: Mumps IgG — immunity marker. Reported qualitatively (Immune/Non-Immune) or as an assay-specific titer; immune is favorable. No universal numeric band (assay-specific).

biomarkers.name: Varicella Zoster Antibody IgG
biomarkers.note: Varicella-zoster (chickenpox) IgG — immunity marker. Reported qualitatively (Immune/Non-Immune) or as an assay-specific titer; immune is favorable. No universal numeric band (assay-specific).

biomarkers.name: Trisomy 21 Screen
biomarkers.note: Prenatal cell-free-DNA screen for trisomy 21 (Down syndrome). A low-/high-risk screen, not a diagnosis — a high-risk result is confirmed by diagnostic testing. No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: Trisomy 18 Screen
biomarkers.note: Prenatal cell-free-DNA screen for trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome). A low-/high-risk screen, not a diagnosis. No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: Trisomy 13 Screen
biomarkers.note: Prenatal cell-free-DNA screen for trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome). A low-/high-risk screen, not a diagnosis. No numeric band.

biomarkers.name: Fetal Fraction
biomarkers.note: Fraction of cell-free DNA in a NIPT draw that is fetal (a run-quality metric, typically ≥4% for a valid result). A QC value, NOT a health signal — never flagged.

biomarkers.name: Glucose, Gestational Screen (50 g)
biomarkers.note: 1-hour 50 g glucose challenge (GCT) — gestational-diabetes screen. A value ≥ the lab's cutoff (here 135 mg/dL) prompts the diagnostic 3-hour OGTT. Distinct from fasting/random Glucose.

biomarkers.name: Peak Expiratory Flow
biomarkers.note: Peak expiratory flow (PEF) — the fastest speed you can blow out, in litres per minute, from a peak-flow meter. Deliberately carries NO population band: an action plan reads a blow as a percentage of your OWN personal best (green ≥80%, yellow 50–80%, red <50%), so the zone is computed against your recorded best and there is no verdict without one. National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute / GINA asthma action-plan zones.

biomarkers.name: Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second (FEV1)
biomarkers.note: Forced expiratory volume in one second, in litres — the air you can force out in the first second of a full blow, measured by spirometry. No fixed band: normal is a percent of the value predicted for your height, age and sex, so it is trended as an absolute series and read beside the FEV1/FVC ratio. American Thoracic Society / European Respiratory Society.

biomarkers.name: Forced Vital Capacity (FVC)
biomarkers.note: Forced vital capacity, in litres — the total air you can force out after a full breath in, measured by spirometry. No fixed band, for the same reason as FEV1: normal is a percent of a height/age/sex-predicted value. American Thoracic Society / European Respiratory Society.

biomarkers.name: FEV1/FVC Ratio
biomarkers.note: The proportion of your forced vital capacity blown out in the first second, as a percentage. The one spirometry value with a universal cutoff: a post-bronchodilator ratio under 70% is the fixed criterion for persistent airflow obstruction, whatever your height or age. Screening context, not a diagnosis. GOLD / ATS-ERS.

biomarkers.name: Urine Color
biomarkers.note: Color of the urine specimen on the physical exam of a urinalysis (straw, yellow, amber, red). Qualitative — it shifts with hydration, diet and medications, so there is no normal band.

biomarkers.name: Urine Appearance
biomarkers.note: Clarity of the urine specimen (clear, hazy, cloudy). Qualitative; cloudiness can come from cells, crystals, mucus or a contaminated collection.

biomarkers.name: Bacteria, Urine
biomarkers.note: Bacteria seen on urine microscopy. Usually reported semi-quantitatively (none / few / moderate / many) per high-power field; bacteria can mean infection or simply a contaminated collection, so it is read together with the white-cell count and nitrite.

biomarkers.name: Casts, Hyaline, Urine
biomarkers.note: Hyaline casts on urine microscopy, per low-power field. The most common cast type and the least specific — a few are normal after exercise, dehydration or diuretics.

biomarkers.name: Casts, Granular, Urine
biomarkers.note: Granular casts on urine microscopy, per low-power field. A few can follow exercise or dehydration; persistent numbers suggest tubular injury.

biomarkers.name: Casts, RBC, Urine
biomarkers.note: Red-blood-cell casts on urine microscopy, per low-power field. They point to bleeding from the glomerulus rather than the lower urinary tract, so any are worth attention.

biomarkers.name: Crystals, Urine
biomarkers.note: Type of crystal seen on urine microscopy (calcium oxalate, uric acid, triple phosphate, …). Qualitative — several kinds occur in normal urine and depend on the specimen's pH and how long it sat.

biomarkers.name: Crystal Amount, Urine
biomarkers.note: How many crystals were seen on urine microscopy (few / moderate / many), reported next to the crystal type. Qualitative.

biomarkers.name: Microalbumin/Creatinine Ratio, Urine
biomarkers.note: Urine albumin normalized to urine creatinine (ACR) — the standard way to read a spot urine albumin, because concentration alone tracks how dilute the sample is. KDIGO reads under 30 mg/g as normal and 30–300 as moderately increased albuminuria, but staging needs repeat samples over months, so no flagging band is set here. Uses URINE creatinine — never the serum value.

biomarkers.name: Protein/Creatinine Ratio, Urine
biomarkers.note: Urine total protein normalized to urine creatinine — a spot-sample stand-in for a 24-hour protein collection. Uses URINE creatinine, never the serum value; interpretation depends on the clinical context, so no band is set here.

biomarkers.name: Fecal Occult Blood
biomarkers.note: Screen for blood in the stool (guaiac or fecal immunochemical test). Qualitative — Negative is normal; a positive is a reason to follow up, and the test does not replace a colonoscopy.

biomarkers.name: Stool Color
biomarkers.note: Color of the stool specimen (brown, green, black, red, clay). Qualitative and strongly diet- and medication-dependent.

biomarkers.name: Stool Consistency
biomarkers.note: Consistency of the stool specimen (formed, soft, loose, watery). Qualitative.

biomarkers.name: Stool Ova and Parasites
biomarkers.note: Microscopic examination of stool for parasite eggs (ova) and parasites. Qualitative — None seen is the normal result.

biomarkers.name: Stool Red Blood Cells
biomarkers.note: Red blood cells seen on stool microscopy, per high-power field.

biomarkers.name: Stool White Blood Cells
biomarkers.note: White blood cells (leukocytes) seen on stool microscopy, per high-power field. Their presence suggests an inflammatory or invasive cause of diarrhea rather than a secretory one.

biomarkers.name: Atypical Lymphocytes
biomarkers.note: Reactive (atypical) lymphocytes on the blood smear, as a percentage of white cells. Reported ALONGSIDE the total lymphocyte fraction — a separate value, not a restatement of it — and commonly seen with viral infections.

biomarkers.name: Band Neutrophils
biomarkers.note: Immature (band) neutrophils on the blood smear, as a percentage of white cells. Reported ALONGSIDE the segmented neutrophil fraction — a separate value, not a restatement of it; a rise is the classic left shift of acute infection.

biomarkers.name: Red Blood Cell Morphology
biomarkers.note: The smear reviewer's description of red-cell size, shape and color (normocytic normochromic, anisocytosis, poikilocytosis, …). Qualitative free text that qualifies the numeric red-cell indices.

biomarkers.name: Bilirubin, Indirect
biomarkers.note: Unconjugated (indirect) bilirubin — total minus direct bilirubin. Recorded only when the lab prints it: when either component is reported below its detection limit the subtraction is undefined and labs print Can't Calc rather than guess, which is why this is not computed here.

biomarkers.name: HDL as % of Cholesterol
biomarkers.note: HDL cholesterol expressed as a percentage of total cholesterol, printed by some lipid panels. A higher share is generally more favorable, but it is read with the absolute values rather than against a band of its own.

biomarkers.name: Omega-6 Total
biomarkers.note: Total omega-6 fatty acids as a percentage of total fatty acids by weight. It counts species the panel does not itemize (DGLA and minor omega-6s), so it is NOT the sum of the printed arachidonic and linoleic acid lines.

biomarkers.name: Antinuclear Antibody Screen, Indirect Immunofluorescence Assay (ANA IFA)
biomarkers.note: Antinuclear antibody screen by indirect immunofluorescence (IFA) — the first-line test for autoimmune connective-tissue disease. Qualitative (Negative / Positive); a positive is normally followed by a titer and a staining pattern, and low-level positives are common in healthy people.

biomarkers.name: PR Interval
biomarkers.note: Time from the start of atrial depolarization to the start of the ventricular QRS, in milliseconds — how long the electrical signal takes to cross from the atria to the ventricles. Normal in adults is 120–200 ms; longer is first-degree AV block, shorter suggests pre-excitation. AHA/ACCF/HRS 2009 recommendations for the standardization and interpretation of the electrocardiogram.

biomarkers.name: QRS Duration
biomarkers.note: How long the ventricles take to depolarize, in milliseconds. Normal adult QRS is about 70–100 ms and 110 ms is the usual upper limit; wider than that points to a bundle-branch block or another intraventricular conduction delay. Only the upper bound is banded — a short QRS is not a finding. AHA/ACCF/HRS 2009 ECG standardization recommendations.

biomarkers.name: QT Interval
biomarkers.note: Time from the start of the QRS to the end of the T wave, in milliseconds — the whole ventricular depolarization-plus-recovery cycle. Deliberately carries NO band: the raw QT shortens as heart rate rises, so the same 400 ms is normal at 60 bpm and prolonged at 100 bpm. The rate-corrected QTc is the value that is read against a threshold, and it is curated separately. AHA/ACCF/HRS 2009 ECG standardization recommendations.

biomarkers.name: QTc Interval
biomarkers.note: The QT interval corrected for heart rate (usually by Bazett), in milliseconds — the ECG value that actually carries the clinical weight here. Prolongation is the actionable finding: ≥450 ms in men and ≥460 ms in women is prolonged, and ≥500 ms marks a substantially raised risk of torsades de pointes. Several common medications are monitored with it. Only the upper bound is banded; the rare short-QT syndromes are not screened for this way. AHA/ACCF/HRS 2009 recommendations for the standardization and interpretation of the electrocardiogram, Part IV (ST segment, T and U waves, and the QT interval).

biomarkers.name: P Axis
biomarkers.note: The average direction of atrial depolarization in the frontal plane, in degrees — an orientation, not an amount. The conventional normal arc in adults is 0° to +75°; outside it suggests a non-sinus atrial rhythm or lead misplacement. A wide arc, so a value near either edge is not by itself meaningful. AHA/ACCF/HRS 2009 ECG standardization recommendations.

biomarkers.name: QRS Axis
biomarkers.note: The average direction of ventricular depolarization in the frontal plane, in degrees. The conventional normal arc in adults is −30° to +90°; more negative is left axis deviation and more positive is right axis deviation, both of which are read alongside the rest of the tracing rather than on their own. AHA/ACCF/HRS 2009 ECG standardization recommendations.

biomarkers.name: T Axis
biomarkers.note: The average direction of ventricular repolarization in the frontal plane, in degrees. Deliberately carries NO band: unlike the P and QRS axes it is not read against an absolute arc but against the QRS axis it sits beside — a wide frontal-plane QRS–T angle is the finding, and that comparison is made on the tracing. Trended as a dated series only. AHA/ACCF/HRS 2009 ECG standardization recommendations.

biomarkers.name: Ventricular Rate
biomarkers.note: How many times the ventricles contracted per minute during the ECG recording. Normal is 60–100/min. It is the ECG's own measured rate and is kept separate from resting heart rate on purpose: in atrial fibrillation or flutter the ventricular rate is the response to a much faster atrial rate, so the two are genuinely different numbers on the same tracing. AHA/ACCF/HRS 2009 ECG standardization recommendations.

biomarkers.name: Electrocardiogram (ECG) Interpretation
biomarkers.note: The reading clinician's overall verdict on an ECG, in words ("normal sinus rhythm", "sinus bradycardia", "anterior infarct, age undetermined"). Qualitative — a judgement rather than a measurement, so it carries no reference band and never flags; it is kept as a dated timeline beside the intervals the same tracing measured.

biomarkers.name: Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI), Left
biomarkers.note: Left ankle systolic pressure divided by the higher brachial (arm) pressure — a unitless ratio screening for peripheral artery disease. 1.00–1.40 is normal, 0.91–0.99 borderline, ≤0.90 abnormal and diagnostic of PAD, and above 1.40 means the vessels are too stiff to compress rather than healthy. Kept as a separate series from the right leg. AHA 2012 scientific statement on measurement and interpretation of the ankle-brachial index.

biomarkers.name: Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI), Right
biomarkers.note: Right ankle systolic pressure divided by the higher brachial (arm) pressure — a unitless ratio screening for peripheral artery disease. 1.00–1.40 is normal, 0.91–0.99 borderline, ≤0.90 abnormal and diagnostic of PAD, and above 1.40 means the vessels are too stiff to compress rather than healthy. Kept as a separate series from the left leg. AHA 2012 scientific statement on measurement and interpretation of the ankle-brachial index.

biomarkers.name: Cardio-Ankle Vascular Index (CAVI), Left
biomarkers.note: A blood-pressure-independent measure of arterial stiffness from the heart to the left ankle, reported as a unitless index. Under 8.0 is normal, 8.0–9.0 borderline, and 9.0 or above suggests arteriosclerosis; it rises with age. Kept as a separate series from the right side. Device criteria of the VaSera oscillometric method (Shirai et al., J Atheroscler Thromb).

biomarkers.name: Cardio-Ankle Vascular Index (CAVI), Right
biomarkers.note: A blood-pressure-independent measure of arterial stiffness from the heart to the right ankle, reported as a unitless index. Under 8.0 is normal, 8.0–9.0 borderline, and 9.0 or above suggests arteriosclerosis; it rises with age. Kept as a separate series from the left side. Device criteria of the VaSera oscillometric method (Shirai et al., J Atheroscler Thromb).

biomarkers.name: Fat Mass Index
biomarkers.note: WHOLE-BODY fat mass divided by height squared — the fat half of body composition expressed the way BMI is, so it is comparable between people of different heights. The normal-fat range is 3–6 kg/m² in men and 5–9 kg/m² in women; above it is excess fat and below it is fat depletion. Sex-specific by nature, so no sex-neutral band is drawn. Schutz, Kyle & Pichard, Int J Obes 2002; NHANES DXA reference values, Kelly et al., PLoS ONE 2009.

biomarkers.name: Lean Mass Index
biomarkers.note: WHOLE-BODY lean (fat-free) mass divided by height squared — trunk and head included, which is what separates it from the Appendicular Lean Mass Index, the arms-and-legs-only measure sarcopenia thresholds are defined on. Carries no fixed band: it is read as an age- and sex-specific percentile against DXA reference data rather than against a cutoff. NHANES DXA body-composition reference values, Kelly et al., PLoS ONE 2009.

biomarkers.name: Metabolic Equivalents (METs)
biomarkers.note: Peak functional capacity reached on an exercise test, in metabolic equivalents — multiples of resting energy use, where 1 MET is about 3.5 mL/kg/min of oxygen. No population reference band, because the expected value depends on age and sex; the prognostic reading is broad instead — under 5 METs is poor capacity, 5–10 moderate to good, and 10 or more is excellent, which is the optimal target carried here. ACC/AHA exercise-testing guidance; FRIEND registry reference standards.

biomarkers.name: Exercise Stress Test Result
biomarkers.note: The supervising clinician's overall verdict on an exercise stress test, in words ("negative for ischemia", "positive", "non-diagnostic — target heart rate not reached"). Qualitative — a judgement rather than a measurement, so it carries no reference band and never flags; it is kept as a dated timeline beside the capacity the same test measured.

biomarkers.name: Color Vision
biomarkers.note: The examiner's verdict on a colour-vision screen such as the Ishihara plates ("normal", "red-green deficiency", "12/14 plates correct"). Qualitative — a judgement rather than a measurement, so it carries no reference band and never flags; most colour-vision deficiency is inherited and lifelong, so the value rarely moves.

biomarkers.name: Audiologic Diagnosis
biomarkers.note: The audiologist's verdict on a hearing evaluation, in words ("normal hearing bilaterally", "mild high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, left"). Qualitative — a judgement rather than a measurement, so it carries no reference band and never flags; the per-ear, per-frequency thresholds it summarises are curated separately and are what the audiogram surface plots.
